text:
Macklin Celebrini won it in overtime, and the Sharks needed him to. San Jose trailed Montreal by two goals and came back to beat the Canadiens 4-3 at Centre Bell. Celebrini scored the first goal of the night in the opening period, assisted on Tyler Toffoli's tying power-play goal late in the third, then finished it on another power play 2:13 into overtime. He ended with two goals and an assist.

Montreal had the better of the play for most of the night. The Canadiens outshot San Jose 77 attempts to 51 and held the edge in expected goals (the quality of chances, not just their number), 3.68 to 3.05. In a simulation that replays every shot many times, Montreal wins 60 percent of the time. The second period was theirs: goals from Juraj Slafkovský and Cole Caufield built a 3-1 lead on a 1.43 to 0.71 chance advantage. Goalie Jakub Dobes allowed 0.95 goals more than the shots he faced would normally produce, and the Sharks got to him when it counted. Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 31 of 34 for San Jose, saving 0.68 goals more than expected.

Special teams settled it. San Jose scored on two of its three power plays and Montreal went 0 for 2. Montreal's Nick Suzuki, Slafkovský and Caufield each finished with a goal and an assist, and that was not enough on a night the Canadiens could not hold a two-goal lead. The facts here give no streaks or records for either team, so the result stands on its own: a comeback win for the Sharks and a game that got away from Montreal.
